notes: Declared beliefs on the parameter each model's long run turns on, one default per entity class (24): long-run growth on the DCF-shaped paths and (58) the long-run return on equity on the residual-income path. Six fields per belief and nothing else: mean, sd, floor, ceiling, why, as_of; a truncated normal. Values in percentage points as offsets around the country's settled terminal growth in params.json (mean 0 = the country's terminal growth; floor -2 = two points below it), so one default serves every currency.

Never estimated from history by the tool. The why may cite history, GDP or base rates as evidence; the numbers are a declaration, dated, revised by a dated declaration when evidence warrants, never because of what a number looks like.

The belief parameter is fixed on the merits, not for convenience. On the DCF-shaped paths it is terminal growth: starting growth is observed from filings, the reversion speed is a structural assumption with its sensitivity shown, and long-run growth is the question every investor can answer. On the residual-income path (58) it is the long-run return on equity the ROE path reverts to, for the same reason: roe_0 is observed, lambda is the structural assumption, and whether a franchise earns above its cost of equity forever is the question. Either choice may be revisited only on an argument about the model, never on what it does to a number.

Bank and Insurer carry a belief since 58, centred on the cost of equity. Before that they carried none, because the residual-income path has no terminal growth; the answer was not to give it one but to name the parameter it does have.

The first four defaults were confirmed by the user as of 2026-09-19. Bank and Insurer were added as drafts on 2026-09-23 and confirmed by the user the same day (63), which also raised their ceilings from three points over the cost of equity to eight and from two to five, the centre, the width and the floor untouched. No default is a draft now.

names: per-name beliefs, absolute in percentage points (the name's long-run nominal growth), same six fields, tracked here beside the class defaults; a name's entry overrides its class default. None declared yet.

correlation (35): the joint distribution of the beliefs is a Gaussian copula with one declared common-factor correlation for every pair (optional per-pair overrides under pairs, each exactly a, b, rho, why, as_of), mapped through each name's truncated normal. The user confirmed common = 0.20 on 2026-09-20 as the book's assumption, the declaration itself dated 2026-09-19; it is revisable by a dated declaration, never estimated from prices or history.

Bank and Insurer (58) are offsets over the COST OF EQUITY, not over terminal growth: the residual-income path has no terminal growth, and the parameter the belief is about is the long-run return on equity the ROE path reverts to. A zero mean is therefore the declaration that the long run grants no franchise value, which is brief 15's anchor; only the width and the ceiling say a franchise might hold above the cost of equity. These two were confirmed by the user on 2026-09-23, as the first four were, and their ceilings were raised to eight points over the cost of equity for a bank and five for an insurer (63): a ceiling of three said a large bank cannot sustain more than three points over in the long run, and franchise banks have held five to eight points over for decades. The revision is an argument about the world, never about the probability the belief assigns to a price -- it moved probability_overpaid on none of the nineteen residual-income records.

OperatingCompany.why: long-run growth near the economy's; a mature business does not outgrow it forever

HighGrowthSoftware.why: same centre, wider: the long run is further away and less certain

Cyclical.why: wider below: the product's long-run demand is the risk

Reit.why: rent growth tracks inflation; a narrow ceiling

Bank.why: the centre is the cost of equity and grants no franchise; the ceiling admits one because franchise banks have held five to eight points over their cost of equity across decades, an observed pattern, not a result; a bank priced for more than eight points over is priced for something the belief does not hold

Insurer.why: the same, narrower: underwriting cycles turn and a hard market does not persist, but a franchise insurer has held three to five points over across cycles

correlation.why: the book's assumption between Apple and JPM: long-run growth rates share the world economy but the businesses differ; one number for every pair until a pair earns its own
